major_concerns: Deterministic verifier completeness uncertain (false negatives may hide unsafe behavior).
Synthetic topology/CLI set may not capture production diversity (external validity).
Single-model evaluation limits claims of generality; prompt sensitivity not addressed.
Repair-loop budget/stop criteria could lead to oscillation or excessive model calls.
required_design_repairs: Assess verifier coverage (add multiple verifiers or known-ground-truth tests) and report verifier limitations.
Expand topology/vendor diversity or justify representativeness; include dataset specification for reproducibility.
Include prompt-sensitivity ablation and evaluate at least one alternate LLM or prompt variant.
Preregister repair iteration budget, retry policy, and stopping rules; include model-call budget accounting.

major_concerns: Design statement implies using verifier-derived features pre-repair (logical inconsistency: verifier output requires running verifier on generated config).
Risk of overfitting to verifier-specific failure signatures; may not generalize to other verifiers.
Cost and latency of running verifier at scale may limit practical deployment; dataset collection may be constrained.
required_design_repairs: Clarify precisely which features are available at prediction time (only LLM-side signals vs light-weight static checks) and ensure no leakage from future-repair steps.
Evaluate generalization by training/ testing across different verifier implementations or holding out verifier assertion types.
Provide cost/latency analysis for verifier runs and simulate deployment scenario (pre-commit vs post-commit checks).
Prespecify train/val/test splits and use bootstrap/DeLong tests as planned; include calibration analysis.

major_concerns: Automated perturbation operators may produce unrealistic or unnatural intents (threat to construct validity).
Results likely sensitive to chosen LLM/prompt; prompt-sensitivity needs control.
Large operator × seed matrix increases model-call and analysis complexity; power analysis missing.
required_design_repairs: Define and justify perturbation operator taxonomy; include human validation of realism for a subset of perturbations.
Include prompt-sensitivity controls (alternate prompts/models) or show robustness metrics across at least one alternate model/prompt.
Perform a power/sample-size analysis to justify 400 seeds and per-operator coverage; prespecify multiple-comparison corrections.
Add mitigation/defense baseline(s) (e.g., verifier-feedback or constrained prompting) to make results actionable.

major_concerns: Fine-tuning may be infeasible on hosted models or exceed available compute/policy constraints (practical execution risk).
Synthetic dataset of three vendors may not capture real-world CLI idiosyncrasies (external validity).
'Operationally acceptable accuracy' is unspecified (ambiguous success criterion).
required_design_repairs: Verify fine-tuning capability on target model(s); if unavailable, replace fine-tune arm with simulated continued-instruction-tuning via in-context or lightweight local models and document differences.
Specify acceptability thresholds in advance (e.g., target verifier-pass rate) and justify them with operational references or expert input.
Improve dataset realism: include more vendors or real CLI snippets, document vendor-specific idioms, and ensure verifier alignment across vendors.
If fine-tuning retained, include compute-cost estimate and fallback plan (few-shot/adapter tuning) in preregistration.
